addressed.instructions: Read `item.text` for this directive from `anchor.statement`: on a sanity FAIL below the round cap the sanity close hook reopens the checked bead to its assignee and sends that dev the sanity-fail.xml.j2 template naming each undone deliverable on the dev's still-open task, creating no finding bead, new layer or new task. Answer yes only when the item itself states that content. Answer no when the item is silent, mentions the subject without that content, or plans a different approach (for example it creates finding beads, a new layer or a new task instead). Do not judge conflict.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` says on a sanity FAIL below the round cap the sanity close hook reopens the checked bead to its assignee and sends that dev the sanity-fail.xml.j2 template naming each undone deliverable on the dev's still-open task, creating no finding bead, new layer or new task. Does `item.text` plan any of these: (1) creating finding beads or child beads for a sanity FAIL; (2) cutting a new layer or branch for the fix; (3) creating or assigning a new ATM task for the fix; (4) not reopening the checked bead on a FAIL that is below the round cap? Silence is never a conflict. Also not a conflict: silence about FAIL handling; escalating to the lead without reopening when a FAIL reaches max_sanity_rounds, because the statement covers only FAILs below the cap; incrementing the round counter. Judge conflict only.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
